# Automatic module name

There can be cases where the project must be built with only Java 8 and thus
cannot take advantage of
[JEP 238: Multi-Release JAR Files](https://openjdk.org/jeps/238). In this case,
it is recommended to define the module name in the `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file.
While the Java module system can determine the module name automatically from
the JAR file name, that is less than ideal as the file name can easily change.
Also, providing the module name would eliminate any guess work as the module
name will be simply read from the `Automatic-Module-Name` entry in the
`META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file.

This simple example shows how to provide the module name in the
`META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file using the [Maven](https://maven.apache.org/) build
tool.

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>${maven-jar-plugin.version}</version>
    <configuration>
        <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}/libs</outputDirectory>
        <archive>
            <manifest>
                <mainClass>${project.mainClass}</mainClass>
            </manifest>
            <manifestEntries>
                <Automatic-Module-Name>custom.module.name</Automatic-Module-Name>
            </manifestEntries>
        </archive>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8)

- [Oracle Java 11](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java11)

## Run the example

1. Build the application (using Java 1.8)

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the classes were created

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name './target/classes'
   ```

   The main class for this simple application

   ```
   ./target/classes
   └── demo
       └── Main.class

   2 directories, 1 file
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── automatic-module-name.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

2. Verify the class byte code version

   ```shell
   javap -v './target/classes/demo/Main.class' | grep major
   ```

   This will print the bytecode major version.

   ```
     major version: 52
   ```

3. Describe the JAR file

   The `--describe-module` flag is not available in Java 8. Switch to Java 11+.
   Assuming that the environment variable `JAVA_11_HOME` contains the path to
   the Java 11 home directory.

   ```shell
   "${JAVA_11_HOME}/bin/jar" --describe-module --file './target/libs/automatic-module-name.jar'
   ```

   This will print the module’s description.

   ```
   No module descriptor found. Derived automatic module.

   custom.module.name automatic
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo
   main-class demo.Main
   ```

   The automatic module name is the name that we defined in the `pom.xml`
   `maven-jar-plugin` plugin configuration.

   ```xml
   <plugin>
       <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
       <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
       <version>${maven-jar-plugin.version}</version>
       <configuration>
           <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}/libs</outputDirectory>
           <archive>
               <manifest>
                   <mainClass>${project.mainClass}</mainClass>
               </manifest>
               <manifestEntries>
                   <Automatic-Module-Name>custom.module.name</Automatic-Module-Name>
               </manifestEntries>
           </archive>
       </configuration>
   </plugin>
   ```

   (*Optional*) Read the manifest file within the JAR file.

   ```shell
   unzip -p './target/libs/automatic-module-name.jar' 'META-INF/MANIFEST.MF'
   ```

   This will print the contents of the manifest file

   ```
   Manifest-Version: 1.0
   Automatic-Module-Name: custom.module.name
   Java-Version: 8
   Build-Jdk-Spec: 1.8
   Created-By: Maven JAR Plugin 3.5.1
   Main-Class: demo.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   The `--module-path` flag is not available in Java 8. Switch to Java 11+.
   Assuming that the environment variable `JAVA_11_HOME` contains the path to
   the Java 11 home directory.

   ```shell
   "${JAVA_11_HOME}/bin/java" --module-path './target/libs' --module custom.module.name
   ```

   This will print the following message

   ```
   Automatic Module Name
   Using Java 11.0.32.1
   ```
